name: WV-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+20 partisan lean in a Trump-era state
Incumbent Riley Moore with a large fundraising edge
No polls and minimal outside spending signal a low-attention race
Prediction markets price the Democrat at about 3%
model.rationale: WV-02's R+20 lean, Moore's incumbency and roughly five-to-one fundraising advantage over Ace Parsi, and markets pricing the race at 97% Republican all point to a safe Republican hold with no offsetting evidence.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or a polling surprise showing Parsi within single digits would warrant a downgrade toward Likely R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Riley Moore, the Republican incumbent, seeks a second term in a West Virginia district that leans about twenty points Republican at the presidential level. His challenger, Democrat Ace Parsi, has raised roughly $250,000 and holds about $115,000 on hand, while Moore has raised over $1.3 million with more than $750,000 available. No outside groups have meaningfully engaged on either side.

No public general-election polls exist, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive. Prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a 3% chance of winning. The fundamentals, money, and market pricing all align: this is a safe Republican seat, with the only realistic path for Democrats being a dramatic, unobserved shift in the race's attention and resources.
